titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Entry into Jerusalem in Glory (ch. 107)
part: ch. 107 — the entry into Jerusalem in glory
about: The chapter heading names Christ's entry into Jerusalem in glory, and the text answers with a chain of prophecies in the frame "and as X prophesied and said": Isaiah, Zechariah, David, Solomon and Ezra, then Jacob's blessing of Judah (the lion's whelp, the sceptre that does not depart). The author then explains that "Beloved", "Messiah" and "Jesus" all name Christ, cites the Ascension of Isaiah and the psalms of the unicorn's horn, and ends with Habakkuk's "horns in his hands" read as the nails of the cross.

sentences.i: Chapter 107: Concerning the entry into Jerusalem in glory
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በአቱ is the noun 'entry, entrance' (from በአ 'enter') in the construct before ኢየሩሳሌም, so 'the entry of/into Jerusalem' (?); the reference is Christ's entry into Jerusalem, as the prophecies below make clear. በስብሐት is በ- 'in' + ስብሐት 'glory, praise'. Geʿez proofed against HaCohen's Unicode Bezold text.

And-as prophesied Zechariah prophet and-said: 'Rejoice-you(f), rejoice-you(f), daughter-of Zion, and-let-exult Jerusalem in-joy.' And-as prophesied David and-said: 'From-mouth-of children and-infants you-prepared praise on-account-of enemy, that you-put-down the-enemy and-the-avenger.' And-as prophesied Solomon and-said: 'Children-your taught with God, and-will-rejoice nations within-you(f).' And-as prophesied David father-his and-said: 'Blow-you(pl) horn in-Zion on-day-of rising, on-marked day feast-our, for ordinance-his for-Israel it.' And-as prophesied Ezra scribe and-said: 'Go-out-you(pl), make-you(pl) feast in-gladness, and-say-to-her to-daughter-of Zion: Rejoice-you(f), behold king-your(f) has-arrived.' And-as prophesied Isaiah prophet and-said: 'Rejoice-you(f) Jerusalem, rejoice-you(f), behold king-your(f) has-arrived, while he-rides upon ass, he-whose-reward with-him and-work-his before face-his.' sentences.i: And concerning the entry into Jerusalem in glory the prophets prophesied. Isaiah the prophet said: 'Shine, shine, Jerusalem! Your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen over you.' And as Zechariah the prophet prophesied and said: 'Rejoice, rejoice, daughter of Zion, and let Jerusalem exult in joy.' And as David prophesied and said: 'Out of the mouth of children and infants you have prepared praise, because of the enemy, to put down the enemy and the avenger.' And as Solomon prophesied and said: 'Your children are taught by God, and the nations will rejoice within you.' And as his father David prophesied and said: 'Blow the horn in Zion on the day of the rising (?), on the appointed day of our feast, for it is an ordinance for Israel.' And as Ezra the scribe prophesied and said: 'Go out, keep a feast with gladness, and say to the daughter of Zion: Rejoice! Behold, your king has come.' And as Isaiah the prophet prophesied and said: 'Rejoice, Jerusalem, rejoice! Behold, your king has come, riding on an ass, he whose reward is with him and whose work is before his face.' And as David the prophet prophesied and said: 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.'
sentences.n: This long unit has no ፤ or ። inside it, so it is kept whole as cut by script. It opens a catena of prophecy for Christ's entry into Jerusalem (the Palm Sunday scene), strung on the frame ወበከመ ተነበየ X ወይቤ 'and as X prophesied and said' (ወ- 'and', በ- + ከመ 'as'; perfect ተነበየ, tä-stem of n-b-y). The quotations and their sources: Isaiah 60:1 ('Shine, Jerusalem, your light has come'; አብርሂ is the feminine imperative, -ኪ the feminine 'your'); Zechariah 9:9 ('Rejoice, daughter of Zion'); Psalm 8:2 (the mouths of children and infants, quoted in Matthew 21:16 at this very entry); ምሁራን 'taught' is Isaiah 54:13 ('your children taught of the Lord'), which the text gives to Solomon, and the 'nations rejoicing in you' is a different verse again, so this is a loose citation; Psalm 81:3 (80:4 in the Septuagint), the horn blown on the feast, given to 'David his father'; Ezra the scribe is credited with a saying that echoes Nehemiah 8 and Zechariah 9:9, not a verse I can match (?); then Isaiah again with the king on an ass (Zechariah 9:9, with 'his reward is with him and his work before him' from Isaiah 40:10 / 62:11); and Psalm 118:26 (117:26), 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord', which the crowds cry in Matthew 21:9. Source slip kept as printed: ን ፡ ጉሥኪ is one word, ንጉሥኪ 'your king', split by a stray wordspace (ንጉሥኪ is spelled whole earlier in this unit). Uncertain: ሠርቅ 'rising' (sunrise, new moon?) in 'day of the rising' (?); እምርት is 'sign, mark', so 'marked/appointed day'; ወበልዋ is ወ- + imperative 'say to her' (በል- + suffix -ዋ). ዘዕሴቱ 'he whose reward' is ዘ- 'who/whose' + ዕሴት 'reward' + -ሁ.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ሰብሑከ ፡ አኀዊከ ፡ እደዊከ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ዘባኖሙ ፡ ለጸላእትከ ፡ ወይሰግዲ ፡ ለከ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ እምከ ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Jacob son-of Isaac and-said: 'Judah, they-praised-you brothers-your; hands-your upon necks-their of-enemies-your; and-they-will-bow to-you children-of mother-your;
sentences.i: And as Jacob the son of Isaac prophesied, he said: 'Judah, your brothers have praised you; your hands are on the necks of your enemies; and the sons of your mother will bow down to you;
sentences.n: Genesis 49:8, Jacob's blessing of Judah, here read as a prophecy of Christ from Judah's line. ሰብሑከ is the perfect ሰብሐ 'praise' with the suffix -ከ 'you'; ዘባኖሙ 'their necks' is ዘባን + -ሙ, and ለጸላእትከ is 'of your enemies' with the ለ- of possession. ወይሰግዲ is printed with the ending -ዲ, not the usual plural -ዱ; I read it as 'they will bow' (?), with ደቂቀ 'sons of' in the accusative form as its subject, so the parse is uncertain (?).

sentences.t: ወኢየሐጽጽ ፡ ምልክና ፡ እምይሁዳ ፡ ወምስፍና ፡ እምአባሉ ፡ እስከ ፡ አመ ፡ ይረክብ ፡ ዘጽኑሕ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወውእቱ ፡ ተስፋሆሙ ፡ ለአሕዛብ ።
sentences.l: and-not will-fail sceptre(?)-your from-Judah, and-rule from-limbs-his, until when he-finds that-which-reserved for-him; and-he hope-their for-nations.
sentences.i: and kingship will not fail from Judah, nor rule from his loins, until he comes for whom it is reserved; and he is the hope of the nations.
sentences.n: Genesis 49:10, the 'sceptre shall not depart from Judah'. ምልክና (from ምልክ, 'kingship, dominion') and ምስፍና ('rule, governorship') are both abstract nouns in -ና; the first is printed with the ending -ና, which I take as the plain noun 'kingship' (?), not 'your kingship'. አባል is 'limb, loin' (the Hebrew has 'from between his feet'). ይረክብ ዘጽኑሕ ሎቱ is literally 'he finds that which is reserved for him'; the Septuagint's 'until there come the things reserved for him' stands behind it, so ዘጽኑሕ is 'he/that which is kept' (?). The last clause, 'and he is the hope of the nations', is the Septuagint's 'and he is the expectation of the nations' (the Christian reading).

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ጸዐዳ ፡ ስነኒሁ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘበረድ ፡ ወፍሡሓት ፡ አዕይንቲሁ ፡ ከመ ፡ ወይን ፡ ወየኀፅብ ፡ በወይን ፡ ልብሶ ፡ ወበደመ ፡ አስካል ፡ ሶንዶኖ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ወልደ ፡ አንበሳ ፡ ሰከብከ ፡ ወኖምከ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘያነቅሆ ፡ አላ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ እስከ ፡ ይረክብ ፡ ዘነዐወ ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-prophesied and-said: 'White teeth-his like that-of hail(?), and-glad eyes-his like wine, and-he-washes in-wine garment-his, and-in-blood-of cluster robe-his.' And-again he-prophesied while he-says: 'Judah son-of lion, you-lay-down and-slept-you; there-is-not who-wakes-him except himself, until he-finds he-who prevailed(?);
sentences.i: And again he prophesied and said: 'His teeth are white like hail (?), and his eyes are glad like wine, and he washes his garment in wine, and his robe in the blood of the grape.' And again he prophesied, saying: 'Judah, son of a lion, you lay down and slept; there is no one who can wake him but himself, until he comes who has prevailed (?);
sentences.n: Genesis 49:12 and 49:9. The two ወካዕበ ተነበየ 'and again he prophesied' (ካዕበ 'again, a second time') mark that the same patriarch is quoted a second and third time. በረድ is 'hail, ice' (the Hebrew and Greek have 'milk' for the teeth), so 'white like hail' (?). ፍሡሓት 'glad, bright' is a feminine plural adjective on አዕይንት 'eyes'. ሶንዶኖ is the Greek loanword σινδών 'linen cloth, robe' with the suffix -ኦ; አስካል is 'cluster of grapes'. In the second quotation ሰከብከ ወኖምከ is 'you lay down and slept' (Genesis 49:9); ዘያነቅሆ 'who wakes him' is ዘ- + ያነቅሆ (ʾa-stem of n-q-h 'be awake'). ዘነዐወ is, I think, 'he who prevailed' (ነዐወ 'conquer', as in Revelation 5:5, 'the Lion of the tribe of Judah has prevailed'), but this is uncertain (?).

sentences.t: እምሕዛእትከ ፡ ዕርግ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ ባረኮ ፡ ለይሁዳ ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ህሎ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ዘይወፅእ ፡ እምኔከ ፡ ዘየኀፅብ ፡ በወይን ፡ ልብሶ ፡ ወክቡር ፡ ምዕራፊሁ ፡ ለፍቁር ፤
sentences.l: from-shoot-your(?) you-went-up. And-again he-blessed-him Judah son-of Jacob and-said-to-him: 'There-is king who goes-out from-you, who washes in-wine garment-his, and-honoured resting-place-his for-the-Beloved;
sentences.i: 'From your shoot (?) you went up.' And again he blessed Judah the son of Jacob and said to him: 'There is a king who comes out of you, who washes his garment in wine; and honoured is his resting-place, for the Beloved;
sentences.n: Genesis 49:9–12 continues (Judah the lion's whelp, 'from the shoot, my son, you went up'). ሕዛእት (here with the preposition እም- and -ከ) I take as 'shoot, sprout' (?). ባረኮ is the perfect ባረከ 'bless' plus -ኦ 'him'; ወይቤሎ is 'and he said to him'. ህሎ ንጉሥ 'there is a king' (ህሎ 'there is/was'). ምዕራፍ is 'resting-place, abode' (also 'end'), so 'his resting-place is honoured'. ለፍቁር 'for the Beloved' is a Christian addition to the verse: ፍቁር 'beloved' (from ፈቀረ 'love') is the title the next units explain. The ፤ ends mid-sentence; the explanation of ፍቁር follows.

The first of three glosses. ብሂል is the infinitive of በሀለ 'say' used as a gloss-marker, 'to say' = 'that is to say, which means'. So: 'Beloved' stands for 'Christ'. ክርስቶስ is the Greek-derived 'Christ', anointed. The sequence of ብሂል clauses is a teacher's equation of the three names; flag the pattern once, it recurs in the next unit.

sentences.t: ወመሲሕ ፡ ብሂል ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ብሂል ፡ ወኢየሱስ ፡ ብሂል ፡ መድኀኔ ፡ ሕዝብ ፡ ብሂል ፤
sentences.l: and-Messiah to-say Christ to-say, and-Jesus to-say saviour-of people to-say;
sentences.i: and 'Messiah' means 'Christ', and 'Jesus' means 'Saviour of the people';
sentences.n: Same ብሂል gloss formula. መሲሕ (Hebrew mashiach 'anointed') is equated with ክርስቶስ (Greek christos 'anointed'); ኢየሱስ 'Jesus' is explained as መድኀኔ ሕዝብ 'saviour-of people' (construct chain; መድኀኒ 'saviour' from ድኅነ 'be saved'). The explanation of Jesus as 'Saviour' echoes Matthew 1:21.

sentences.t: ወነቢያትሰ ፡ ይሰምይዎ ፡ በሥውር ፡ ለክርስቶስ ፡ ወይብልዎ ፡ ፍቁር ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዕርገቱ ፡ በትንቢት ፡ ውእተ ፡ አሚረ ፡ ይወርድ ፡ ፍቁር ፡ እምሰማይ ፡ ወየኀሪ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ፲ወ፪ ፡ ሐዋርያት ፤
sentences.l: And-the-prophets-indeed they-name-him in-secret to-Christ, and-they-call-him Beloved. And-said Isaiah at ascension-his in-prophecy: 'That day will-descend the-Beloved from-heaven and-will-choose for-him twelve apostles;
sentences.i: The prophets, for their part, name Christ in secret and call him 'the Beloved'. And Isaiah said, in a prophecy about his ascension: 'On that day the Beloved will come down from heaven and choose for himself twelve apostles;
sentences.n: The enclitic -ሰ in ወነቢያትሰ marks contrast ('the prophets, for their part, ...'). ይሰምይዎ and ይብልዎ are 3mp imperfects with the object suffix -ዎ 'him' (ሰመየ 'name', በሀለ 'say/call'). በሥውር 'in secret' (ሥውር 'hidden'). ኀበ ዕርገቱ 'concerning/at his ascension' (ኀበ 'at'). The quotation is not in the canonical Isaiah but in the Ascension of Isaiah (3:13–18, 'the Beloved will descend from the seventh heaven and choose twelve apostles'), a work preserved whole in Geʿez. ወየኀሪ ሎቱ is 'and he will choose for himself' (ኀረየ 'choose'); ፲ወ፪ is the numeral 12, 'twelve'; ሐዋርያት 'apostles'.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ርኢኩ ፡ ዕርገቶ ፡ ለፍቁር ፡ ወልድ ፡ እስከ ፡ ሳብዕ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ ይትቄበልዎ ፡ መላእክት ፡ ወሊቃነ ፡ መላእክት ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይትሌዐል ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ እምኔሆሙ ።
sentences.l: And-again he-said: 'I-saw ascension-his of-the-Beloved Son up-to seventh heaven, and-while they-receive-him angels and-chiefs-of angels, while he-exalts-himself exceedingly above-them.'
sentences.i: And again he said: 'I saw the ascension of the Beloved Son up to the seventh heaven; and while angels and archangels were receiving him, he was exalting himself exceedingly above them.'
sentences.n: Again the Ascension of Isaiah (chapters 9–11), the prophet's vision of the Beloved's ascent through the heavens to the seventh. ሊቃነ መላእክት 'chiefs-of angels' = archangels (ሊቅ 'chief', construct plural ሊቃነ). ይትቄበልዎ is the tä-stem 'they receive him' (ተቄበለ), reciprocal-reflexive in sense 'welcome'; ይትሌዐል is 'he is exalted, raises himself' (?), the tä-stem of ልዕለ 'be high'. ፈድፋደ is the accusative adverb 'exceedingly'.

sentences.t: ወዳዊትኒ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ወፍቁርሰ ፡ ከመ ፡ ወልድ ፡ ዘ፩ቀርኑ ፤
sentences.i: And David too said: 'And the Beloved is like the son of the unicorn;
sentences.n: Psalm 29:6 (28:6 in the Septuagint): 'the beloved like a son of unicorns'. ዘ፩ቀርኑ is ዘ- 'who' + the numeral 1 + ቀርኑ 'his horn', 'the one who has one horn', the unicorn (Greek monokerōs). The numeral stands inside the word as printed. -ኒ 'too' and -ሰ 'indeed' are enclitics. Note the psalmist's 'beloved' is read as Christ, as just explained.

sentences.i: And again he said: 'And from the horns of the unicorn, for my humility;
sentences.n: Psalm 22:21 (21:22 in the Septuagint): 'save me from the horns of unicorns, my humility'. The text gives only the end of the verse, and ለብሕቱትየ 'for my lowliness' (ብሕቱት 'humility, lowliness' (?), with ለ- and -የ 'my') is kept close to the Greek 'my humble state'.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ወይትሌዐል ፡ ቀርንየ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘ፩ቀርኑ ፡ አቅርንትሰ ፡ ይተረጐም ፡ መንግሥታተ ፡ ዓለም ፡ ወዘይትበህልሂ ፡ ዘ፩ቀርኑ ፡ ለመንግሥቱ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘይትቃረኖ ፡ እስመ ፡ መላኬ ፡ ነገሥት ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ ይስዕር ፡ ወለዘፈቀደ ፡ ይሠይም ፡ በከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወእምክቡዳነ ፡ አቅርንት ፡ ዘእምኔሆሙ ፡ ኣስተፈሥሐከ ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-said: 'And-he-will-be-exalted horn-my like that-of the-one-horned.' The-horns-indeed are-interpreted kingdoms-of world, and-that-which-is-said-also 'of-the-one-horned' for-kingdom-his there-is-not who opposes-him; for ruler-of kings he, to-him who wished he-overthrows, and-to-him-who-wished he-appoints; as said David: 'And-from-honoured horns, of-whom they-made-glad-you;
sentences.i: And again he said: 'And my horn will be exalted like that of the unicorn.' (Psalm 92:10) The horns, now, are interpreted as the kingdoms of the world; and as for what is called 'the unicorn's', there is no one who opposes his kingdom, for he is the ruler of kings: whomever he wishes he overthrows, and whomever he wishes he sets up. As David said: 'And from the honoured horns, from whom they made you glad (?);
sentences.n: Psalm 92:10 (91:11 in the Septuagint), 'my horn shall be exalted like the unicorn's'. Here the author stops to interpret the symbol: አቅርንት 'horns' stand for መንግሥታተ ዓለም 'kingdoms of the world' (ይተረጐም 'is interpreted', passive of ተረጐመ 'translate, interpret'), while the lone horn of the unicorn means one unrivalled kingdom. ዘይትበህልሂ is ዘ- + the tä-stem 'what is said' + -ሂ 'also'; ዘይትቃረኖ 'who opposes him' (ተቃረነ 'oppose' (?)). መላኬ ነገሥት 'ruler of kings' (መላኪ 'ruler', construct). ይስዕር 'overthrows' (ሰዐረ 'defeat') and ይሠይም 'appoints' (ሠየመ). The closing quotation is Psalm 45:8 (44:9 in the Septuagint), 'from ivory palaces they have made you glad', reshaped to speak of horns; ዘእምኔሆሙ 'of whom, from whom' and ኣስተፈሥሐከ (with the printed variant ኣ for አ) 'they made you glad', ʾa-stem of ተፈሥሐ, is uncertain in form (?). The ፤ ends the unit mid-sentence; the comment on the quotation follows.

sentences.t: ወዝንቱ ፡ ዘተብህለ ፡ እምክቡራን ፡ ነገሥት ፡ አንተ ፡ ትከብር ፡ ወትትፌሣሕ ፡ ብሂል ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ እንባቆም ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ አቅርንት ፡ ውስተ ፡ እደዊሁ ፡ ወረሰየ ፡ ፍቁረ ፡ በጽንዐ ፡ ኀይሉ ፤
sentences.l: And-this which-was-said from-honoured kings: 'You are-honoured and-you-rejoice,' to-say. And-as prophesied Habakkuk while he-says: 'Horns in hands-his, and-he-set the-Beloved in-firmness-of power-his;
sentences.i: And this is what was said concerning the honoured kings: 'You are honoured and you rejoice' — that is what it says. And as Habakkuk prophesied, saying: 'Horns are in his hands, and he set the Beloved in the firmness of his power;
sentences.n: ዘተብህለ 'which was said' is the passive ተብህለ. The quotation 'you are honoured and rejoice' is the sense of the Psalm 45:8 line just given, read as addressed to the honoured kings; the ብሂል at the end is the same 'that is to say' marker. The next is Habakkuk 3:4, 'horns [rays] in his hands, and he set the love of his strength' (Septuagint: he made a strong love of his might); the Geʿez makes ፍቁረ the accusative 'the Beloved' (ረሰየ 'set, make'). In the Hebrew the 'horns' are rays of light; the text takes them as symbols again. በጽንዐ ኀይሉ 'in the firmness of his power' (construct chain: ጽንዕ 'firmness', ኀይል 'power').

sentences.t: ወዘንተኒ ፡ ብሂል ፡ አኃዜ ፡ ስልጣነ ፡ ነገሥ ፡ ት ፡ በቅንዋት ፡ ተቀነወ ፡ እራኁ ፡ ዘሕይወተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ውስቴቶን ፡ እኁዝ ፡ ዘገብረ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ በጽንዐ ፡ ኀይሉ ፡ ፍቁር ፡ ብሂል ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-this-also to-say: holder-of authority-of kings with-nails was-nailed, ʾərāḫu(?) he-whose life-of all within-them held, which made Christ in-firmness-of power-his, the-Beloved, to-say.
sentences.i: And this too it says: the holder of authority over kings was nailed with nails, his ... (?), he in whom the life of all is held; what Christ made in the firmness of his power is 'the Beloved'.
sentences.n: A hard final unit; the sense is the Christian reading of Habakkuk's 'horns in his hands': the nails of the cross in the hands of the crucified king. Source slip kept as printed: ነገሥ ፡ ት is one word, ነገሥት 'kings', split by a stray wordspace (so አኃዜ ስልጣነ ነገሥት, construct chain 'holder-of authority-of kings'). በቅንዋት ተቀነወ 'with nails he was nailed' (ቅንዋት 'nails', passive ተቀነወ). እራኁ is not a form I can parse; it may be a corrupt or rare word, left as 'his ... (?)'. ውስቴቶን is 'within them' (feminine plural), most likely the nails or horns; እኁዝ 'held'. The final clause I read as 'what Christ made in the strength of his power — that is called the Beloved' (?). The trailing ፨ ፨ ፨ is the edition's closing ornament, kept on this unit.
